newsitem.title: USA: Mobil held talks on downstream,nothing new.
newsitem.headline: Mobil held talks on downstream,nothing new.

text.p: Mobil Corp said that it has held talks with several oil companies about its U.S. downstream operations, but none of these has reached the stage which warrants comment, a spokesman for Mobil said.

Earlier today, Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette analyst John Hervey issued a report that said Mobil was close to announcing a downstream joint venture with Amoco Corp which could generate $700 million in annual savings for the two companies combined.
This drove Mobil stock up 3-9/16 to 76-7/16 and Amoco up 2-1/4 to 95-3/4.
Hervey said that he had spoken to a Mobil employee who said he expected the merger to be announced within two weeks.
However, a spokesman for Mobil said that while it continued to evaluate options for its U.S. downstream operations, no announcement was imminent.
"We are continually looking for ways to improve all our businesses around the world, including refining and marketing in the U.S.," he said.
"The alliance with British Petroleum Co Plc in Europe is a case of where things were right," the spokesman added.
Talk of a merger between Mobil and Amoco has been doing the rounds for some time, and resurfaced in May.

The U.S. downstream industry has been plagued by poor returns on capital and this has seen Shell Oil Co, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, merge its U.S. operations with those of Texaco Inc, while companies such as ARCO and Unocal Corp have exited the business altogether.
Mobil is still examining its options, as are several other companies which have not formed joint ventures, Amoco among them.
"If we saw the the right opportunity we woould not hesitate to have discussions with interested parties," said teh Mobil spokesman.
No one from Amoco was immediately available for comment. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
